Provide guidance after checking both the published floor-by-floor facilities and temporary operation notices.
Do not infer the scope of nonpublic construction.
Do not infer the results of on-site inspections.
Cleaning and security contractor staff prefer service routes separated from general users during shift changes.
The main entrance lobby is on the first floor of the Main Building.
The visitor services desk is on the first floor of the Main Building.
The Innovation Hub is on the first floor of the Main Building.
A general restroom is on the first floor of the Main Building.
An accessible restroom is on the first floor of the Main Building.
The elevator lobby on the second floor of the Main Building is near the student support administration office.
The elevator lobby on the third floor of the Main Building is near the corridor toward the Central Library.
The names of the department offices on the fourth floor of the Main Building are displayed on the floor directory.
A shared printing station available to students is on the fourth floor of the Main Building.
The research labs on the fifth floor of the Main Building are not spaces open to the general public.
The collaborative research lab on the sixth floor of the Main Building is used by authorized research members.
Consultations with the research support office on the seventh floor of the Main Building follow the posted appointment process.
Visitors to staff offices on the eighth floor of the Main Building expect the staff member with whom they have an appointment to be in the office at the scheduled time.
Public administrative services on the ninth floor of the Main Building are provided during each department's operating hours.
The elevators in the Main Building connect the underground parking level through the tenth floor.
The floor directory agent can describe the floors and space names of published facilities.
The floor directory agent cannot check the current occupancy status of meeting rooms.
First-time visitors are more familiar with department names than floor numbers and can more easily understand directions centered on department names.
On public holidays, some administrative offices may not operate even when the Main Building is open.
The floor directory agent cannot verify in real time, at the time of an inquiry, whether published floor-by-floor information matches the actual layout.
Add campus-wiki/route-changes: The indoor route that passed through the first through third floors of the Main Building to the Central Library cannot be used during the construction period.
Add campus-wiki/route-changes: The route from the third-floor rear entrance to the Central Library is closed during the construction period.
Add campus-wiki/route-changes: The Outdoor Parking Lot A–Main Building–Central Library route is closed during the construction period.

Modify campus-wiki/route-changes: A student who prefers the air-conditioned indoor route through the Main Building in summer may experience substantial heat and travel burden when redirected to an outdoor alternative route during the construction period.

Add campus-wiki/route-changes: When providing directions to the accessible restroom in the Student Centre during the construction period, instruct users to take the accessible route to the left as viewed from the Main Building.

Add campus-wiki/route-changes: During the construction period, the designated alternative accessible route to the Central Library is Outdoor Parking Lot C–Student Centre accessible entrance–Central Library west entrance.

Add campus-wiki/route-changes: During the construction period, the Central Library west entrance is designated as the official alternative entrance for the closed connecting route through the Main Building.

Modify campus-wiki/route-changes: During the construction period, the route guidance agent may exclude from comparison candidates closed routes that pass through the first through third floors of the Main Building, the third-floor rear entrance, or Outdoor Parking Lot A.

Modify campus-wiki/route-changes: If the indoor shortcut through the Main Building is closed during the construction period, a mobility-support companion may reconfirm the distance and slope of the alternative accessible route before accompanying the user.

analysis.overview: The frames jointly support cautious construction-period navigation while serving different roles: one supplies the Main Building directory and agent limits, and the other supplies temporary closures, alternatives, accessibility directions, and travel impacts. Their overlapping guidance is complementary or explicitly condition-scoped, with no unresolved contradiction.

relations.reason: The explicit construction-period condition distinguishes temporary route availability from durable landmark and layout information.
relations.summary: Published Main Building landmarks support the Central Library connection, while construction-period guidance temporarily closes the affected indoor and rear-entrance routes and designates the library west entrance as the alternative.

relations.reason: The construction condition narrows the general notice-checking policy into a temporary route-selection rule.
relations.summary: General directions require checking published facilities and temporary notices, with construction-period guidance specifically permitting known closed routes to be excluded from route candidates.

relations.reason: The specific published closure and the prohibition on extrapolating beyond disclosed construction jointly govern reliable construction routing.
relations.summary: A stated construction-period closure may guide routing without supporting inferences about undisclosed construction scope.
